unit.label: Stomach trouble & help
unit.title: Stomach Trouble and Getting Help
unit.description: Describe stomach trouble, offer or decline help, and sequence a completed event with 就.

goal.pinyin: Wǒ péi nǐ qù kànbìng, hǎo bu hǎo?
goal.meaning: I'll go with you to see a doctor, okay?

lessons.title: What Is Wrong?
lessons.subtitle: Use a concern question and describe someone's complexion.

steps.explanation: 怎麼了 is the condition-inquiry question taught here.
臉色 refers to the look/color of someone's face.
難看 describes looking bad here.

steps.prompt: Why does 你怎麼了？ fit this scene?
options: It asks with concern about the person's condition.
It asks how many times something happened.
steps.answer: It asks with concern about the person's condition.
steps.explanation: That is the concern/condition function of 怎麼了？

steps.audioText: 你怎麼了？臉色這麼難看。
steps.prompt: What observation follows the concern question?
steps.explanation: 臉色這麼難看 describes the person's appearance.

lessons.title: Stomach Trouble
lessons.subtitle: Describe stomach discomfort and repeated vomiting.

steps.explanation: 肚子 means stomach/abdomen.
吐 means vomit.
次 counts occurrences.

steps.prompt: In 好幾次, 幾 means…
steps.explanation: This directly retrieves the Unit-46 semantic expansion.
好幾次 is a statement meaning several times.

steps.audioText: 肚子很不舒服，還吐了好幾次。
steps.prompt: Which two problems do you hear?
steps.explanation: The audio combines 肚子很不舒服 with 吐了好幾次.

lessons.title: Right After Doing It
lessons.subtitle: Sequence a completed event and its immediate result.

steps.prompt: Which sentence means “After taking medicine, he immediately went to sleep”?
options: 他一吃了藥以後，就睡覺。
steps.explanation: V了…就… marks completed event 1 followed immediately by event 2.

steps.prompt: Which version correctly uses 以後?
options: 他一吃了藥以後，就睡覺。
steps.explanation: The completed-event + 就 pattern allows 以後.

steps.prompt: How should the completed-event + 就 pattern normally form a question in this lesson?
options: with 嗎 or 是不是
with an ordinary A-not-A of the first verb
steps.answer: with 嗎 or 是不是
steps.explanation: Ordinary A-not-A is not used for this pattern.

options: 一…就… favors a short first verbal phrase; V了…就… can take a fuller completed first event
V了…就… cannot use 以後
一…就… requires a completed-action 了
steps.answer: 一…就… favors a short first verbal phrase; V了…就… can take a fuller completed first event
steps.explanation: That is the key contrast.

steps.prompt: In 吃了東西就吐, what is the first completed event?
steps.explanation: The first event is eating something; vomiting follows.
就 introduces the immediate next event.

lessons.title: I Will Go With You
lessons.subtitle: Offer to accompany someone to see a doctor.

steps.explanation: 陪 means accompany.
看病 means see a doctor.

steps.prompt: What is the speaker offering to do?
options: accompany the person to see a doctor
steps.answer: accompany the person to see a doctor
steps.explanation: 陪你去看病 is an offer of help.

steps.prompt: What does 好不好 do here?
options: checks whether the listener agrees to the helpful proposal
steps.answer: checks whether the listener agrees to the helpful proposal
steps.explanation: This retrieves the earlier proposal/agreement use.

steps.prompt: Which helpful action do you hear?
steps.explanation: The offer is to accompany the listener to see a doctor.

lessons.title: Health Insurance and the Health Center
lessons.subtitle: Politely decline help and discuss insurance/health-center options.

steps.prompt: 不用 了 is best understood here as…
steps.explanation: This is a polite refusal.
健康 means health.
保險 means insurance.
健康中心 means health center.

steps.prompt: In 對學生也很客氣, who receives the politeness?
steps.explanation: 對 + person marks the person toward whom someone is polite.

steps.prompt: What does 買藥就好了 express here?
steps.explanation: Here V + 就好了 means that doing the action will be enough.

steps.audioText: 我在臺灣沒有健康保險。
steps.prompt: What does the speaker say they do not have?
steps.explanation: The sentence says the speaker has no health insurance.

lessons.title: Health Check-In
lessons.subtitle: Integrate the health episode and complete the four-question health call.

steps.prompt: Which sequence best matches the episode?
options: notice bad complexion → hear stomach/vomiting symptoms → offer to accompany → help is declined → suggest health center → pharmacy preferred
ask duration → compare rent → read a prescription → discuss weather
buy medicine → ask about typhoons → compare actions → refuse food
steps.answer: notice bad complexion → hear stomach/vomiting symptoms → offer to accompany → help is declined → suggest health center → pharmacy preferred
steps.explanation: This is the communicative arc of the health episode.

steps.prompt: Which question asks where the person feels unwell?
steps.explanation: This is one of the four required health-condition questions.
發燒 is the fever vocabulary from Unit 45.
This asks about the throat condition.
This asks about appetite.

options: that the person really will not see a doctor
that the person slept several hours
steps.answer: that the person really will not see a doctor
steps.explanation: The question confirms refusal to go see a doctor.

options: It may use 以後 and does not use ordinary A-not-A.
It is identical to 一…就… in every restriction.

newVocabulary.note: Ask this when someone seems unwell or something seems wrong: “What’s wrong?”
The color or appearance of someone’s face, especially as a sign of health or emotion.
Not good to look at. Describing 臉色, it means the person looks unwell, not that you are insulting their appearance.
The belly or abdomen; 子 is pronounced with a neutral tone: dùzi.
Pronounced tù (fourth tone) for “vomit; throw up.”
Counts occurrences of an action: 三次 means “three times.” It does not measure how long the action lasts.
Go or stay with someone, often to keep them company or help: 陪你去看病.
To see a doctor as a patient. Learn the phrase together rather than translating 看 as “look at.”
Politely decline an offer: “No need, thanks.” It does not mean that something is broken or unusable.
Health; also healthy in descriptive uses. 健康中心 is a health center.
Insurance. 健康保險 means “health insurance.”
A health center, such as the place on campus where students can seek care.

臉.note: 臉 means “face.” 臉色 liǎnsè is someone’s facial color or complexion, which can show how they feel.
臉.memory: The flesh component 月 is on the left and the wider 僉 is on the right. A face is part of the body.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: flesh component
parts.description: This four-stroke 月-shaped component relates to the body.

parts.label: 僉
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Keep the paired lower shapes under the broad top of 僉.

肚.note: 肚 appears in 肚子 dùzi, “belly; abdomen.” The 子 syllable is neutral-tone zi in this word.
肚.memory: Put flesh 月 next to 土. The body component helps distinguish 肚 from the mouth character 吐.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: flesh component
parts.description: The four-stroke body component sits on the left.

parts.label: 土
parts.name: earth component
parts.description: The three-stroke 土 sits on the right.

吐.note: 吐 is tù, fourth tone, when it means “vomit.” Learn this reading in the illness context.
吐.memory: Mouth 口 plus 土: remember something coming out of the mouth. Compare 肚, which has 月 instead.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth component
parts.description: The small mouth is on the left.

parts.label: 土
parts.name: earth component
parts.description: Write the three-stroke 土 on the right.

陪.note: 陪 péi means “accompany; go or stay with someone.” 陪你去看病 means “go with you to see a doctor.”
陪.memory: The narrow 阝 stands beside 咅. Keep the left side slim so the right-hand 立-over-口 shape has room.

parts.label: 阝
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The left-side 阝 uses two strokes in this dataset.

parts.label: 咅
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write 立 above 口 to form the right-hand block.

example.meaning: accompany you to see a doctor

健.note: 健 is the first character in 健康 jiànkāng, “health; healthy.” Learn both syllables together.
健.memory: A person 亻 stands beside 建. The person component is a useful cue for a healthy person.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The standing person occupies the left edge.

parts.label: 建
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The eight-stroke 建 fills the right side; its final sweeping stroke runs underneath.

康.note: 康 is the second character in 健康 jiànkāng, “health; healthy.” 健康中心 means “health center.”
康.memory: A broad 广 roof covers the inner strokes. Keep the central vertical visible and the lower strokes balanced.

parts.label: 广
parts.name: outer roof
parts.description: The first three strokes form the roof and left side.

parts.label: 康內部
parts.name: inner strokes
parts.description: Write the eight inner strokes beneath 广, leaving room for the lower spreading strokes.

康.partOrderLabel: outer frame first, then the inside

保.note: 保 means “protect; preserve.” In 保險 bǎoxiǎn, the whole word means “insurance.”
保.memory: A person 亻 stands beside 呆, a 口 over 木. Use the image of a person protecting something as a memory cue.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: Write the two person strokes on the left.

parts.label: 呆
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The three-stroke 口 sits above the four-stroke 木.

險.note: 險 means “danger; risk.” In 保險 bǎoxiǎn, learn the combined meaning “insurance.”
險.memory: The narrow 阝 stands beside 僉. Compare 臉: the right component is shared, but the left component changes.

parts.label: 阝
parts.name: left component
parts.description: This left-side 阝 uses two strokes.

parts.label: 僉
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The thirteen-stroke right side matches the right side of 臉.

u47-vle-jiu.title: V了…就… — do B right after completing A
u47-vle-jiu.explanation: Event 2 follows immediately or very soon after completion of event 1. This pattern can use 以後, contrasts with prior 一…就…, and uses 嗎/是不是 rather than an ordinary A-not-A route.

examples.pinyin: Tā chī le yào jiù shuìjiào.
examples.meaning: After taking medicine, he went right to sleep.

examples.pinyin: Tā chī le yào yǐhòu, jiù shuìjiào.
examples.meaning: After taking medicine, he went to sleep.

examples.text: 妹妹喝了熱湯，就不覺得冷了。
examples.pinyin: Mèimei hē le rè tāng, jiù bù juéde lěng le.
examples.meaning: After younger sister drank hot soup, she no longer felt cold.

u47-vle-jiu.remember: Completed first event + 就 + next event; 以後 is compatible; ordinary A-not-A is not the question route.
